03 / RUN ON THE RECEIVING HOST
Prepare. Connect. Receive.
Unzip the packet and use Linux, Node.js 22.16 or later, Python 3.11 or later, and the existing Stellar Forge toolkit with its native and freighter-wallet features.

    
    
      
  1. PREPARE AND REVIEW
    Open the exact request.
    Restore the captured offer and prepare the original buyer. Replace the toolkit path with the receiving machine’s existing installation or checkout.
    node buyer.mjs prepare --toolkit /ABSOLUTE/EXISTING/TOOLKIT
node buyer.mjs review --toolkit /ABSOLUTE/EXISTING/TOOLKIT
    2. 
      
  2. INITIALIZE ONCE
    Bind the private operator.
    The original operator creates its policy, keys and reservation ledger. Add --payer and the actual public account if it is still empty in the packet.
    node buyer.mjs operator-init --toolkit /ABSOLUTE/EXISTING/TOOLKIT
node buyer.mjs wallet-prepare --toolkit /ABSOLUTE/EXISTING/TOOLKIT
    3. 
      
  3. CONNECT FREIGHTER
    Open the local wallet.
    Start the private server. Open its printed loopback URL in the browser with Freighter, select the intended testnet account, and connect.
    node buyer.mjs wallet-serve --toolkit /ABSOLUTE/EXISTING/TOOLKIT
    4. 
      
  4. EXECUTE AND REOPEN
    Receive the merchant response.
    Run execute in a second terminal. Review the original approval and sign the exact native authorization in Freighter. The request directory retains the actual merchant response and its JSON result view.
    node buyer.mjs execute --toolkit /ABSOLUTE/EXISTING/TOOLKIT
node buyer.mjs result --toolkit /ABSOLUTE/EXISTING/TOOLKIT
node buyer.mjs inspect --toolkit /ABSOLUTE/EXISTING/TOOLKIT
    5.

Bring one real API to its first receiving operator.

One agreed route and response matrix

    
We map the selected query, path and JSON requests, expose their actual payment requirements, and preserve their input and output semantics through approved execution. The receiving operator gets the expected merchant result and payment outcome; interruption and reopening continue the same saved work. A second operator completes the delivered installation and walkthrough with the agreed account and API.

    
Inputs and delivery plan

    
Rail provides its technical contact and selected facilitator/network. The merchant supplies the real API or documented extension point, receiving account, sample requests, intended response contract and release owner. Days 1–2 confirm that contract; days 3–5 complete the adapter and buyer flow; days 6–8 run the selected merchant/account operation and recovery; days 9–10 deliver the agreed installation and operator handoff. Hosting, service usage and payment charges stay on the commissioning party’s accounts.

    
Rail can commission the work directly or introduce a merchant for a jointly scoped engagement. These three captured requests follow Rail’s original demonstration contracts; the launch uses that selected merchant’s real API.
